chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah Amir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalah ibn Ayyub, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

'When you pray salat and you are facing other than the Qiblah, and it becomes clear to you that you prayed facing other than the Qiblah, and you are still within the prayer time, then repeat it. But if the prayer time has passed, do not repeat it.'

key_terms.أَعِدْ: repeat/redo — obligation to repeat the prayer within its valid time
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: Qiblah — the direction of the Ka'bah in Mecca which Muslims face during prayer
key_terms.فَاسْتَبَانَ: it became clear/evident — refers to discovering or realizing one's error
key_terms.وَقْت: prayer time — the prescribed window within which a specific prayer must be performed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone prays in the wrong direction (not facing the Qiblah)?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a clear legal ruling on prayers performed facing the wrong direction. If a person discovers their error while the prayer time still remains, they must repeat the prayer correctly. However, if the time has already elapsed, the prayer is considered valid and need not be repeated. This ruling reflects the Islamic jurisprudential principle of balancing the obligation of correct prayer performance with the mercy of not imposing undue hardship once the time has passed.
